target_customer: Remote workers, freelancers, creators and small businesses in emerging markets (initially Nigeria and Kenya) paid by foreign clients
problem: Workers in emerging markets struggle to receive foreign currency pay, hold it, and convert it to local currency; Grey provides USD, EUR and GBP accounts, conversion, cards and transfers.
business_model: Fees and foreign exchange spread on conversions and transfers, virtual cards, plus a business product (Grey Business)
product_category: Cross border payments and multi currency accounts

founders.name: Idorenyin Obong
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as an ex Paystack employee; education not found.

founders.name: Femi Aghedo
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder and COO by TechCrunch (Aug 2022); the YC page lists only the CEO. Background not covered.

competitors.name: Verto
competitors.what: Global B2B payments platform giving African businesses multicurrency wallets for international payments

competitors.name: PayDay
competitors.what: Techstars backed service with similar cross border offerings

technical_complexity.rationale: Multi currency accounts via partner banks, FX conversion, payouts to bank accounts and mobile money, virtual cards and stablecoin transfers across multiple African regulators; moderate engineering plus compliance.

defensibility.rationale: Habit and balance holding create some stickiness, but competitors like Verto and PayDay offered similar products and rails come from partner banks.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copy found; later growth to over 1 million users by 2024 per a Launch Base Africa headline.

market_need_then: Remote work for foreign clients grew and Nigerians needed to convert foreign currency to naira; Grey started in July 2020 as an instant exchange service and had about 100,000 users by August 2022.

branding.name_origin: Company said Grey was inspired by the colour and conveys stability, neutrality and solidity in financial services (per rebrand coverage).

identity.logo: New corporate logo and website redesign introduced at the Feb 2022 rebrand
identity.visual_style: Neutral grey palette, per the name rationale
identity.voice_and_tone: Approachable fintech language for remote workers

branding.brand_signature: The rebrand from Aboki Africa to the single color word Grey

rebrands.why: Company said it had outgrown the currency exchange mission and expanded beyond Nigeria.

branding.community_and_virality: Several African tech outlets covered the rebrand and a TechCabal list of Africa's biggest tech rebrands includes it; no merch or fan evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Short, memorable name and visible rebrand coverage across African tech press; generic color word is hard to search and no evidence of viral brand pull.

pivots.from: Aboki Africa: instant exchange of foreign currency to naira
pivots.to: Grey: foreign accounts, cross border payments and business accounts
pivots.why: Outgrew the exchange only mission and expanded beyond Nigeria (rebrand coverage).

outcome_analysis: Grey began in 2020 as an instant exchange service for Nigerians, rebranded in February 2022 around foreign accounts, joined YC, and raised a 2M seed in August 2022 with about 100,000 users and 200 percent volume growth in 2022. A 2024 headline reports over 1 million users. Searches found no layoffs, shutdown or regulatory action, so it appears to have grown with the remote work and cross border payment wave.
notes: Seed of 2M USD in Aug 2022 is stated by TechCrunch and Finextra's press release coverage. An undisclosed pre-seed in 2021 and an undisclosed raise reported Feb 2022 are not recorded as rounds. Competitors Verto and PayDay come from an Aug 2022 article, about 6 months after the batch, so they are dated after the batch; no earlier dated source was found. Name origin comes from rebrand coverage in search summaries. Founding date varies (July 2020 per TechCrunch, 2021 elsewhere). The 1 million user figure is from a headline only.
